annotation.title_clean: Proposal for consensus recommendations in relation to the clarification, consideration and development of aspects of the normative and operational framework on emerging technologies in the area of lethal autonomous weapons systems
annotation.title_en: Proposal for consensus recommendations in relation to the clarification, consideration and development of aspects of the normative and operational framework on emerging technologies in the area of lethal autonomous weapons systems
annotation.authors_or_issuer: International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)
annotation.venue: CCW Group of Governmental Experts on LAWS (CCW/GGE.1/2021/WP.6)
annotation.summary_en: ICRC working paper submitted to the CCW Group of Governmental Experts on lethal autonomous weapons. It sets out humanitarian, legal and ethical concerns and recommends new legally binding rules: prohibit unpredictable autonomous weapons and those targeting humans, and regulate the rest through limits on targets, duration, scope and situations of use, plus human–machine interaction requirements.
key_provisions_or_claims: Prohibit unpredictable autonomous weapon systems whose effects cannot be sufficiently understood, predicted and explained
Prohibit autonomous weapon systems designed or used to apply force against persons
Regulate permitted systems via limits on target types, duration, geographical scope, scale and situations of use
Require human–machine interaction ensuring effective supervision, timely intervention and deactivation
Calls for new legally binding rules clarifying how IHL applies, complemented by policy standards and good practice
